Duncanville sellers can hire an agent, sell alone, or deal with a cash buyer who accepts the house unrepaired. Many decide based on how long a rental or repair headache has gone on.

The city lies in southwestern Dallas County, with 40,706 residents, 14,272 housing units and a homeownership rate of 65.3 percent. Interstate 20 follows the northern edge, Highway 67 marks the east side and a rail line crosses the middle, so some houses back up to traffic or tracks. Buyers notice, so describe and price yours honestly. School assignments come from Duncanville Independent School District, which a buyer's agent will check for the specific address.

  • Agent listing: more buyers see it, at the cost of showings and a lender's timetable.
  • On your own: the fee stays with you, and so do the contract and disclosure duties.
  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies, a faster close and a price that covers repairs.

A single-family house, duplex or townhome with tenants must hold a Rental Certificate of Occupancy before anyone moves in. That is the city's residential rental registration program at work.

An owner registers the property, passes an interior and exterior inspection, and then applies for the certificate. Registration is renewed every year by December 31. The certificate is renewed after two years, when tenants change, or when ownership changes during the registration year. No certificate is issued until taxes, liens, utility charges and code issues are cleared.

That last rule matters if you have tenants. A buyer will ask whether the certificate is current, and open code issues can stall a closing. Call the Permitting Department at (972) 780-5000 to request an inspection.

Confirm amounts with the Permitting Department before you pay, because the city's master fee schedule controls.

Duncanville residential rental program charges
ChargeAmount
Registration, inspection and certificate$150.00
Change of tenant registration$125.00
Second reinspection, same violation$100.00
Late fee, each 30 days after due date$100
Replacement certificate$25
Penalty for not registeringClass C misdemeanor, fine up to $2,000

Schedule the inspection within 30 days of registration or of a failed inspection, or a $50 late fee applies. A failed property gets 30 days to correct violations, and the first reinspection is free. Inspectors look at the roof, walls and foundations, plumbing, electrical and mechanical systems, pests, and nuisance items such as high grass, junk and inoperable vehicles.

Start with the registration, then the inspection record, then the tenant. Owners must tell the city two days before an eviction and supply a clean-up plan for personal items within a day afterward, so a sale that involves removing a tenant adds city steps to the court steps.

The eviction process itself comes from state law. Where the lease sets no other period, the landlord serves a written notice to vacate with at least three days' warning, files in justice court, and may obtain a writ of possession six days after final judgment. A buyer who takes a rented house inherits those timelines unless you resolve them first. If the tenant is staying, give the buyer the lease, the deposit amount and the rent history. If the tenant is leaving, set a firm move-out date in writing and walk the unit together so the condition is documented before keys change hands. Take dated photos of each room for your own file.

  • Confirm the certificate is current and the last inspection passed.
  • Write down the lease end date and any deposit held.
  • Tell every buyer in writing about the tenant and any open city notice.

Pull together your registration confirmation, the current certificate and the newest inspection result. A certificate is renewed after two years, on a change of tenant, or on a change of owner within the registration year, so your sale may mean a fresh one for the buyer.

The manager or agent for a registered rental must live or work inside the North Central Texas Council of Governments area, and the unit's maximum occupancy is fixed when it registers. A buyer who plans to hire a distant manager should know that before committing.

  • Copies of every lease and the dates tenants moved in.
  • Receipts for repairs made after a failed inspection.
  • Proof that taxes, liens and utility charges are paid.

Your deed is recorded in Dallas County, while the Dallas Central Appraisal District sets your value. Texas has no statewide property tax, and local units set rates.

A tax bill left unpaid after January 31 is delinquent from February 1. The lien lands on the January 1 owner, which is why the title company pays off the current year when you close. The county clerk records a deed only after the signature has been acknowledged, and the title company can quote the clerk's fees.

Back taxes can sometimes be spread out. Some collectors offer plans of up to 36 months, and a homestead owner may demand one. Check your balance with the Dallas County tax office.

Both situations carry deadlines in Texas, and a sale can still work. Four years is the probate window for a will. Depending on the facts, a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship may do instead, and the buyer's title company has the last word.

Under a federal rule, a lender usually cannot begin foreclosure on a home loan until it is over 120 days delinquent, and a lender has a two-year window to sue for any shortfall. Those limits give a seller some room to act, though a written payoff request is the safest first step.

After a default notice, you may reinstate the loan by paying what is overdue within 20 days. An auction notice follows, and a closing ahead of the sale ends the foreclosure on that loan.

A cash buyer has no lender appraisal to wait for, so loan approval drops out of the schedule. City rules do not disappear, though. If a rental inspection is pending or a reinspection is open, ask the buyer whether they will take the house that way.

If speed is the goal, clear open violations first and close out any failed inspection. A clean file widens the pool of buyers and shortens the questions at closing. Also gather the lease dates and deposit details so a buyer who wants the tenant to stay can decide quickly.

Before you sign anything, confirm in writing who is responsible for the certificate, the registration change and any late fee that may fall due near the closing date. Cash buyers who plan to keep the house as a rental will usually want that settled in the contract, and a clear answer helps them make an offer faster.

faqs.a: Yes. A single-family house, duplex or townhome with tenants has to register and carry a Rental Certificate of Occupancy.

faqs.q: How often must a Duncanville rental be inspected?
faqs.a: At first registration, then every two years from the certificate, or sooner when tenants change.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for skipping Duncanville rental registration?
faqs.a: A Class C misdemeanor, with a fine of up to $2,000, separate from any other code violations.
The city's schools belong to Duncanville Independent School District. Ask the district about the zone for a particular address.

faqs.q: Can a buyer rent out a Duncanville house by the night?
faqs.a: The rental registration program covers rentals of more than 30 days, so a stay-by-the-night plan is a separate question. Call the Permitting Department at (972) 780-5000 for the current rules before you promise anything.
